names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 2 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Κωνσταντίνος ο εξ Αγαρηνών», with the rank word and the phrase «ο εξ Αγαρηνών» left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 2. јун ст. ст., „Свети новомученик Константин“ — Свети is not a rank and новомученик is the `new-martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, so both are stripped and the bare forename is the whole of what the heading leaves. THE SOURCE OFFERS NO FULLER FORM: the island is in the body and not in the heading, so «Mytilene» cannot be carried into the form. The fold is live and deliberate — `foldchk.py` returns `[('constantine-brancoveanu', 'ru'), ('constantine-of-georgia', 'sr'), ('constantine-presbyter-martyr-1918', 'ru'), ('constantine-the-great', 'sr')]` — and the four are told apart by their days, their centuries and their calendars.

death.note: saint.gr's head line reads «Αγιος Κωνσταντινος ο Εξ Αγαρηνων (; - 1819)» and the life ends «τελικά τον απαγχόνισαν στις 2 Ιουνίου 1819 μ.Χ.» The page gives no year of birth.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 2ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Κωνσταντίνος ο εξ Αγαρηνών»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 2 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page names Psilometopo of Mytilene as his village, Magnesia and Smyrna as where his family moved, Mount Athos and the Kavsokalyvia as where Patriarch Gregory V baptised him, Kydonies as where he was seized and Constantinople as where he was hanged; `locations` is left out because the life is a journey between six places and not a residence in one. This is not the corpus's `constantine-the-new-emperor`, an emperor kept on 3 September. The page adds that a manuscript service for him is kept at the Kalyve of Saint John the Theologian in Kavsokalyvia and at the monastery of Saint Panteleimon on Athos.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 15.06.2026 (2. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети новомученик Константин“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, four lines long. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. A SECOND BOOK ON A FOLDER THAT HAD ONE, AND IT GIVES THE BEGINNING THE FIRST DID NOT. saint.gr had the Smyrna fruit shop, the cathedral where he learned the tongue and the religion, the refusal on the Holy Mountain and Patriarch Gregory V’s test. New here: THE HEALING THAT STARTED IT — „Будући исцељен од тешке болести помоћу свете водице у цркви и видећи друга чудеса вере Христове“, healed of a grave illness by the holy water of a church — and THE FORTY DAYS of torment, which the Greek page does not count. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND THE TWO BOOKS AGREE TO THE DAY: saint.gr’s «τον απαγχόνισαν στις 2 Ιουνίου 1819 μ.Χ.» against „обесе у Цариграду 2. јуна 1819. године“. Nothing to widen and nothing to choose; both books give no birth. `types` untouched: новомученик is the `new-martyr` already there and is the only rank word in the heading. The baptism at Kapsokalyvia is corroborated outright, the skete named in both books. No `locations`, no `related` — Patriarch Gregory V is in the prose off saint.gr and is the subject of no martyrdom and no kinship here, and this entry does not name him. A FOLD, DELIBERATE AND ON THE BAREST OF FORMS: `foldchk.py` returns four holders of «Константин», two of them `sr` (`constantine-of-georgia`, `constantine-the-great`), and the heading offers nothing fuller to prefer — no island, no epithet, no see. Stored anyway, as `nikephoros-patriarch-of-constantinople` stored a bare Никифор on this same day, and the fold is recorded as deliberate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Πᾶσαν ηὔφρανας, πιστῶν χορείαν, καί κατήσχυνας, τούς Ἄγαρ γόνους, ἀνακηρύξας λαμπρῶς τήν εὐσέβειαν, καί ὑπομείνας ἀνύποιστα βάσανα, ὦ Κωνσταντῖνε Μαρτύρων ἀγλάϊσμα. Ὡς οὖν ἔτυχες, οὗπερ ἐπόθεις ἀοίδιμε, μνημόνευε ἡμῶν τῶν εὐφημούντων Σε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως, the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Κωνσταντίνος ο εξ Αγαρηνών»

english.text: You gladdened every choir of the faithful and put the sons of Hagar to shame, proclaiming godliness with splendour and enduring torments past bearing, O Constantine, ornament of the martyrs. Since you have obtained, ever-memorable one, the very thing you longed for, remember us who sing your praise.

hymns.text: Φωσφόρος ἀνέτειλε, τῆ Ἐκκλησία Χριστοῦ, ἡ μνήμη τῶν ἄθλων σου, φωτός πληροῦσα αὐτήν, Μαρτύρων ἐκσφράγισμα, ἔνδοξε Κωνσταντῖνε, λύουσα τήν ἀπάτην, γόνων τῶν ἐκ τῆς Ἄγαρ, λάμπουσα δέ πλουσίως, τάς ψυχάς τῶν ἐν πίστει, τήν μνήμην σου τελούντων ἀειμακάριστε.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ΄, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, the second of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Κωνσταντίνος ο εξ Αγαρηνών»

english.text: The memory of your contests has risen like a morning star upon the Church of Christ and filled her with light, O glorious Constantine, seal of the martyrs: it undoes the deceit of the sons of Hagar, and shines richly upon the souls of those who keep your memory in faith, O ever-blessed one.
